newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UNHCR chief calls for help to access Zaire refugees.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR chief calls for help to access Zaire refugees.

text.p: The head of the U.N. refugee agency appealed to the international community on Saturday to help aid agencies provide access to hundreds of thousands of scattered Hutu refugees on the run in east Zaire.

Sadako Ogata told reporters during a meeting of donors and aid chiefs to discuss the crisis that multi-national forces could help agencies find the refugees. "We have no access. I think the international community and those who have the capacity to move in with various advanced modern technology would probably be able to give us some access," she said.
Ogata was speaking as military commanders in Stuttgart, Germany, continued a meeting to discuss an armed intervention force to bring aid to Rwandan and Burundian refugees in Zaire.
Many countries have got cold-feet on a planned multi-national task force in east Zaire after the mass return home of half a million Rwandan Hutu refugees who fled an ethnic Tutsi revolt in the area.
Ogata, asked if she was still pressing for the deployment of the force, said: "If you mean help to find people, where they are, provide access for assistance to them, yes."

She said UNHCR had field information that up to 700,000 refugees were still on the run in east Zaire. "There are quite a few in the northwest part in Masisi area, a congregation between Goma and Bukavu and further west. They are quite far away," said Ogata. "But we cannot get to these peoeple."
